prompt:
A desktop landing page for sqwer, a free touch-typing course for beginners and schools, rendered edge to edge as a finished website screen with crisp readable text, no browser window, no device, no desk.

The visitor is a beginner who has never touch-typed; the page must guide them, room by room, like the wayfinding of a museum's permanent exhibition. The whole page is built from an exhibition signage programme: deep ultramarine enamel wayfinding panels with white type, porcelain-white gallery walls, thin floor-plan linework, museum object labels.

What leads: a great ultramarine entrance panel taking most of the first viewport, with the elegant serif title "Learn to type properly, one key at a time." and a small caption "A typing course for everyone. Free. Starts from zero." Beside it, mounted on the porcelain wall like an exhibit, an illustration of two hands resting on the home row, each finger in its own soft colour, with a museum object label: "Object 1. Where your fingers rest. A S D F and J K L ;". One unmistakable arrow sign: "Get started  →". Below the fold begins a floor plan of the exhibition: twelve numbered rooms on one route, "Room 1 The home row", "Room 2 Reaching up", "Room 3 Reaching down", with a "You are here" marker at Room 1.

Frame: the sqwer wordmark top left, navigation "Learn  Practice  Ranked" set as small sign labels, "Sign in" at the far right. Type voices: a refined high-contrast serif for titles, a clean grotesk for labels, small monospace numerals for room numbers. Corners barely softened, never round.
note: Free-plan output carries an OpenArt watermark.
